functional.text: Continuously ingest new articles (title, snippet, image, URL) from ~50k publishers' RSS/Atom feeds and sitemaps.
Group articles about the same event into one story with a 'full coverage' list; drop near-identical copies.
Show top stories per edition (country + language) and per topic, linking out to publishers.
Personalised 'For you' section from followed topics and reading history.

non_functional.text: Page p99 < 200 ms; read-heavy, with ×5 spikes on breaking news.
Freshness: a breaking story appears within ~5 minutes of first publication.
Highly available reads: serving stale lists is better than an error.
Polite crawling: never overload a publisher.

assumptions.text: ~2M new articles/day; 100M DAU × 5 page views; breaking news ×5.
Keep ~5 KB of metadata per article for a year; full text only 30 days (for clustering).

out_of_scope.text: Full-text search, comments, paywall handling, publisher payouts.

api.notes: Anonymous; cached at the CDN ~30 s.
Batched from the client; feeds interest profiles.

data.name: articles
data.fields: article_id, canonical_url (unique), source_id, title, snippet, image_url, published_at, simhash, embedding, story_id
data.why: Write-once, read by id and by story; ~3.7 TB/year.

data.name: stories
data.fields: story_id, headline, centroid, article_ids, first_seen, last_updated, coverage_count, topic, editions
data.why: Updated as articles join; read by the ranker.

data.name: sources
data.fields: source_id, feed_url, poll_interval, next_due, etag, authority, edition
data.why: Small (50k rows), relational, drives the scheduler.

data.name: ranked lists
data.why: Recomputed every minute; read on every page.

data.name: profiles
data.fields: user_id → topic weights, followed topics, recently seen story_ids
data.why: Read per personalised request; updated from click events.

deep_dives.title: Poll schedule per source

options.name: Same interval for every source
options.cons: either late for wire services or wasteful for blogs

options.name: Adaptive interval: shrink when new items appear, grow when not (1–60 min), WebSub where supported, per-host politeness cap

deep_dives.choice: Adaptive per-source interval (1–60 min) with WebSub pings and per-host rate limits
deep_dives.why: A few hundred sources produce most breaking news; checking them every minute and the long tail hourly fits ~170 fetches/s and keeps N2.

deep_dives.title: Stable story ids when clusters merge or split

options.name: Recompute clusters and ids from scratch each batch
options.cons: links and caches point to vanished ids

options.name: Keep ids; on merge the larger story absorbs the smaller and leaves a redirect

deep_dives.choice: Stable story ids; merges keep the older/larger id and redirect the other
deep_dives.why: Ranked lists, shared links and reader history reference story ids; the hourly re-cluster must not break them.

deep_dives.title: Breaking-news hot story

options.name: Let every request reach origin
options.cons: spike lands on the API and cache

options.name: Short CDN TTL + request coalescing at origin
options.pros: one origin fetch per edition per TTL

deep_dives.choice: 30 s CDN TTL with request coalescing on misses
deep_dives.why: The hot story is on the same edition pages everyone loads, so coalescing collapses the spike to a handful of origin requests.

wrapup.bottlenecks: The clusterer during big news days (partition by language/edition, scale workers), the near-dup index memory (keep 48 h of SimHash bands), CDN misses right after TTL expiry (coalescing).
wrapup.failures: The raw-articles stream buffers fetches if processing lags; pages keep serving the last ranked lists (stale but up); fetchers back off failing hosts; if clustering lags, new articles appear as singleton stories and merge later.
wrapup.monitoring: Publish → visible latency per top source, fetch error rate per host, stream consumer lag, cluster size distribution (too many singletons = threshold drift), page p99, CDN hit ratio.
wrapup.scale: More editions and languages: partition the pipeline by language, add fetchers per region, add ranked lists per edition; profiles shard by user.
wrapup.future: Full-text search, local news by location, fact-check labels, story timelines.

parts.title: Ingestion: finding new articles
parts.problem: Notice new articles from ~50k publishers within minutes (~2M/day, bursts of ~100/s) without overloading small sites or re-downloading unchanged feeds.

options.name: Fixed-interval polling of every feed
options.cons: too slow for wire services, wasteful for weekly blogs

options.name: Adaptive polling per source + WebSub push where offered
options.pros: fast where it matters; few wasted fetches
options.cons: scheduler state per source; push is optional and unreliable alone

options.name: General web crawl of publisher sites
options.cons: huge cost; slow to discover new pages

parts.choice: Adaptive polling per source plus WebSub pings, conditional GETs, fetched articles buffered on a stream
parts.why: Interval follows each source's publish rate, so ~170 fetches/s cover 50k sources and wire services are checked every minute; the stream decouples bursty fetching from slower processing.

parts.title: Dedup and story clustering
parts.problem: Drop syndicated near-duplicate copies and group different outlets' articles about the same event into one story, quickly enough for breaking news.

options.name: Exact hash of URL/body only
options.cons: misses syndicated copies with different boilerplate

options.name: SimHash/MinHash near-dup detection
options.pros: catches copies with small edits in O(1) lookups
options.cons: tuning thresholds; not enough to group different write-ups

options.name: Batch clustering of all recent articles every hour
options.cons: a breaking story waits up to an hour

options.name: Incremental: assign each article to the nearest recent story centroid (embeddings), periodic batch re-cluster
options.pros: seconds of latency; quality repaired in batch
options.cons: story ids can merge/split; needs stable ids

parts.choice: Canonical URL + SimHash to drop copies, then incremental nearest-centroid clustering on embeddings with an hourly batch re-cluster
parts.why: N2 needs a new article placed within seconds; ~23 articles/s × one ANN lookup over ~48 h of stories is cheap, and the batch pass fixes drift.

parts.title: Ranking and personalisation
parts.problem: Order stories for each edition and topic by importance and freshness, and give each logged-in reader a 'For you' section, within the read latency budget.

options.name: Score every story per reader at request time
options.cons: thousands of stories × 29k req/s; no shared caching

options.name: Two stage: precomputed candidate lists per edition/topic, light per-reader re-rank at request
options.pros: shared work done once a minute; personal touch is cheap
options.cons: personalisation limited to the candidate pool

parts.choice: Two-stage ranking: a ranker precomputes top-N lists per edition/topic every minute; the request re-ranks a few hundred candidates with the reader's interest profile
parts.why: Importance (coverage count, source authority, freshness) is the same for everyone, so compute it once; the per-reader part is a dot product over ~300 candidates, well inside N1.

parts.title: Serving the home page
parts.problem: Serve ~6k page views/s, ×5 on a breaking story, in < 200 ms p99, while the underlying lists change every minute.

options.name: Render each page from the stores per request
CDN-cached edition pages (~30 s) + personalised sections blended from cached lists by stateless servers
options.pros: spikes absorbed at the edge; small per-reader work

parts.choice: Edition pages cached at the CDN for ~30 s; a stateless news API behind a load balancer blends personalised sections from cached candidate lists
parts.why: Most traffic is the same edition page, so a 30 s edge cache turns a ×5 spike into a few origin requests per edition; N2's 5-minute budget easily absorbs 30 s.
